title: Cross-boundary sign-off runbook for SSO/RBAC/KMS resilience and evidence mapping
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: Produce a concise, actionable sign-off runbook that maps required evidence artifacts to acceptance criteria for SSO (SAML/OIDC), RBAC, audit logging, and KMS/HSM controls for Private and VPC deployments. Scope includes: assertion replay mitigation, delegated SSO flows, operator roles, scoped key custody, multi-region key replication behavior, retention and tamper-evidence for audit logs, and emergency key-recovery / HSM failover procedures.

Goals: 
- Provide a single source of truth for Engineering, Security, and Customer Success to validate compliance readiness during onboarding and audits.
- Define minimum evidence artifacts and verification steps for each acceptance criterion so sign-off is deterministic.
- Surface open technical gaps and call out mitigation strategies for shipping without blocking customers who need phased acceptance.

Out-of-scope: cryptographic algorithm selection (handled by crypto team RFC), full SOC2 evidence pack generation, and legal contract wording.

Acceptance will require: runbook reviewed by Security, one tabletop exercise of HSM failover with on-call SRE present, and automated smoke test demonstrating RBAC enforcement for at least three operator personas.
acceptance_criteria: SAML/OIDC: documented assertion lifetime and replay protection testcases with passing artifacts (assertion logs, ADFS/IdP traces)
SSO delegated flows: evidence of IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows for sample account; Confluence pages with step-by-step validation and signed-off test checklist
RBAC: least-privilege matrix mapping to IAM roles, sample policy JSONs, and automated role enforcement test that demonstrates 'deny' for a scoped operator persona
Audit logs: retention policy, tamper-evidence proof (hash chain snapshots), and sample query/playbook showing forensic extraction for a 7-day and 90-day scenario
KMS/HSM: key lifecycle runbook including creation, rotation, export policy (no plaintext), multi-region replica behavior, operator access controls, and HSM failover tabletop evidence
Sign-off: Security, Product, and Support must each provide an explicit acceptance note (artifact or comment) before ticket transitions to Done
checklist: Inventory: enumerate all endpoints that accept SAML assertions and document IdP metadata used during onboarding
Threat model: short threat model document covering assertion replay, token theft, and key-exfiltration vectors
Test artifacts: upload SAML trace files, sample assertion XML, and parsed replay detection logs to Drive
RBAC matrix: create CSV of roles->permissions->example API calls and attach to PRD
Automated tests: add CI smoke tests for role enforcement and audit log writability (paths and retention)
KMS keys: create test key in staging KMS, replicate to failover region, and record timing/metrics
HSM tabletop: run simulated HSM node loss, document operator checklist and time-to-recovery
Retention verification: run retention purge job in staging and capture evidence that 30/90-day policies act as expected
Documentation: confluence runbook draft linked and cross-reviewed by Security and Support
Sign-off collection: consolidate sign-off artifacts and comments into a single Evidence ZIP for auditors
updates: 2026-03-12: Ticket created. Initial scoping workshop with Security and SRE. Identified rough evidence surface and required stakeholders: Security (Maya Chen), SRE (Diego Ramos), Support (Priya Shah), and Crypto (Janelle Wu).

2026-03-13: Security requested explicit SAML assertion replay testcases and an expectation doc for max assertion lifetime. Action: Eng to produce assertion-generation harness. Added dependency ENG-1842 for runtime assertion parsing updates.

2026-03-14: Design review (UX) flagged that RBAC error messages exposed to customers should not leak internal role names. Added a small UI work item to ENG backlog and labeled 'low-customer-impact' for rollout phase 1.

2026-03-14: Support ran a spike onboarding flow with a partner account and captured IdP metadata mismatches. Root cause: clock skew tolerance not documented; added test to checklist to validate NTP/Warp9 settings in customer env.

2026-03-15: Draft Confluence runbook uploaded. Security completed initial pass and annotated three non-blocking risks (KMS cross-region latency, HSM operator lockout, audit log hash-rotation cadence). Next step: tabletop HSM failover scheduled for 2026-03-19.
